item.text: {"facts":[{"source_id":"SRC-692e9db1ab8c706d","start_unit":2,"end_unit":3,"fact_summary":"The ASF reported irregularities involving 15.151 billion pesos in Segalmex spending from 2019-2021, including undocumented expenditures, questionable contracts, missing maize, unaccounted Diconsa merchandise, spoiled products, and alleged diversion investigated by the FGR; former finance director René Gavira was in preventive detention and at least one former official was imprisoned.","question_ids":["5B.5","5B.6","5B.7","6B.2","6B.5","6B.7","7B.4","7B.6","7B.7","7B.9","7B.10","8B.3","8B.6","8B.8"],"polarity":"adverse","period_fit":"The article was published in February 2023 and reports mainly 2019-2021 findings and ongoing investigations during 2023.","ruler_attribution":"The reported irregularities occurred in a federal agency created and controlled by López Obrador's government; the source does not establish his personal participation.","limitations":["The article reports audit findings and investigations, not final judicial determinations for every amount or allegation."]},{"source_id":"SRC-a4bf534c33d5eb52","start_unit":2,"end_unit":4,"fact_summary":"López Obrador accelerated inaugurations of major public projects before the March 2024 electoral propaganda restrictions, although the Tren Maya, Mexicana de Aviación, Interoceanic Train, Mexico-Toluca Interurban Train, Tulum airport, and Megafarmacia were in various ways incomplete; the first Tren Maya phase also stopped operations shortly after opening.","question_ids":["4B.2","4B.6","5B.1","5B.6","5B.7","6B.2","7B.1","7B.8","8B.1","8B.2","8B.3","8B.5","8B.6","8B.7","8B.9","8B.10"],"polarity":"mixed","period_fit":"Directly concerns López Obrador's end-of-2023 actions and project status.","ruler_attribution":"The source directly attributes the acceleration and stated electoral timing to López Obrador.","limitations":["The report is journalistic and does not independently quantify all project benefits or long-term outcomes."]},{"source_id":"SRC-b20d11677b724f70","start_unit":2,"end_unit":4,"fact_summary":"López Obrador defended the 2022 reform placing the Guardia Nacional under operational and administrative Army control, arguing that military dependence ensured professionalism, discipline, honesty, and protection; the constitutional challenge argued that public security must remain civilian and exceptional military participation was being made permanent. The article also reports continuing human-rights allegations, including the alleged killing of five unarmed young men by National Guard personnel in Nuevo Laredo.","question_ids":["3B.1","3B.2","3B.4","3B.5","3B.6","3B.8","3B.9","3B.10","4B.4","4B.5","4B.10","8B.2","8B.4","8B.9"],"polarity":"mixed","period_fit":"Reports the April 2023 executive position and contemporaneous allegations.","ruler_attribution":"López Obrador publicly defended and politically supported military control of the Guardia Nacional.","limitations":["The reported Nuevo Laredo killings are described as accusations, not final adjudications."]},{"source_id":"SRC-8e718eb9af053064","start_unit":13,"end_unit":16,"fact_summary":"Human Rights Watch reported escalating violence against journalists, official harassment by López Obrador's daily conferences, near-total impunity, and an underfunded, understaffed federal protection mechanism; at least 33 journalists had been killed since he took office, nine were killed while under federal protection, and the administration proposed an overhaul whose text had not been released.","question_ids":["3B.3","3B.4","3B.7","3B.8","3B.9","3B.10","4B.3","4B.6","4B.9","4B.10","6B.3","6B.5","6B.8","7B.1","7B.2","7B.10","8B.6","8B.8"],"polarity":"adverse","period_fit":"The source is from May 2022 and provides relevant inherited/current context for evaluating 2023, but is not a 2023-year report.","ruler_attribution":"The source directly attributes public harassment to López Obrador and protection-system deficiencies to the federal administration.","limitations":["The source predates 2023 and reports projected or proposed reforms rather than completed implementation."]},{"source_id":"SRC-02fead0b56543145","start_unit":2,"end_unit":4,"fact_summary":"Audits identified unresolved cybersecurity weaknesses across SICT, Sedena, Lotería Nacional, and Pemex. Attacks exposed six terabytes of sensitive military information, disrupted transport licensing and training, and affected refinery operations; deficiencies included obsolete systems, missing patches, weak risk assessment, inadequate monitoring, and failure to correct known vulnerabilities.","question_ids":["1B.3","1B.7","1B.9","1B.10","5B.6","5B.7","6B.5","8B.3","8B.5","8B.6","8B.8","8B.9","8B.10"],"polarity":"adverse","period_fit":"The article was published in November 2022 and describes failures during López Obrador's administration relevant to the 2023 posture.","ruler_attribution":"The failures occurred in federal institutions under López Obrador's government; personal knowledge or direction is not established.","limitations":["The source does not document whether all cited weaknesses remained unresolved throughout 2023."]},{"source_id":"SRC-c49490a20da2f82f","start_unit":2,"end_unit":4,"fact_summary":"The Tren Maya opened in December 2023 as a modern but incomplete project, with unfinished stations, connections, and maintenance facilities. The government had spent about 400 billion pesos, nearly three times the initial estimate, with 74 billion more projected; fares were high relative to regional poverty, and access to some stations lacked public transport. López Obrador assigned operation and security to the armed forces, including four military helicopters and nearly 3,000 National Guard personnel, to keep the asset under national control.","question_ids":["3B.2","3B.6","4B.5","5B.1","5B.6","5B.7","5B.8","6B.2","6B.3","8B.1","8B.2","8B.3","8B.4","8B.5","8B.6","8B.7","8B.9","8B.10"],"polarity":"mixed","period_fit":"Directly concerns the December 2023 opening and contemporaneous costs, access, and operating arrangements.","ruler_attribution":"The source attributes the project's goals, spending choices, armed-forces assignment, and public defense to López Obrador.","limitations":["Projected break-even and poverty-reduction effects had not yet been demonstrated at opening."]},{"source_id":"SRC-fe2838fe23fb7b11","start_unit":2,"end_unit":4,"fact_summary":"The government repeatedly changed the Tren Maya's Section 5 design, including a 42-kilometre elevated section intended to protect karst soil, cenotes, caves, and underground rivers. The changes followed tree clearing and pressure from the hotel sector; a judge suspended construction for lacking an environmental-impact statement, yet López Obrador ordered work to continue. Environmental critics reported that the revised design lacked adequate technical studies, bypassed public participation, and risked ecological damage.","question_ids":["3B.7","3B.9","4B.2","4B.3","4B.4","5B.4","5B.7","6B.3","6B.5","7B.2","7B.7","8B.2","8B.5","8B.6","8B.8","8B.9"],"polarity":"mixed","period_fit":"Reports design and legal decisions made during 2023, including the February announcement and subsequent construction controversy.","ruler_attribution":"The government and López Obrador are directly linked to the design changes, continuation order, and project defense.","limitations":["Environmental and safety risks are partly presented through critics' assessments; the source does not establish eventual realized damage."]},{"source_id":"SRC-6ed0a1a491975e25","start_unit":3,"end_unit":6,"fact_summary":"WOLA reported major discrepancies between military detention figures and entries in the National Detention Registry, indicating that many military arrests may not have been registered. It also reported investigations into torture, cruel treatment, and enforced disappearance involving military and National Guard personnel; absent legally required public use-of-force reports; excessive lethality ratios; and documented practices obstructing truth and justice, including altered scenes, intimidation, and parallel military investigations. WOLA recommended civilian controls, transparency, and compliance with the Supreme Court's April 2023 invalidation of military control of the Guardia Nacional.","question_ids":["3B.1","3B.2","3B.4","3B.5","3B.6","3B.8","3B.9","3B.10","4B.4","4B.5","4B.9","7B.2","7B.6","7B.7","8B.5","8B.6","8B.8","8B.9"],"polarity":"adverse","period_fit":"The report is dated September 2023 and includes 2022 and February-May 2023 administrative data.","ruler_attribution":"The findings concern federal institutions and policies during López Obrador's administration; they do not establish his personal involvement in each abuse.","limitations":["WOLA notes that information-access or transmission limits could partly explain registry discrepancies."]},{"source_id":"SRC-565a605bb42c5a54","start_unit":3,"end_unit":5,"fact_summary":"A Berkeley analysis described López Obrador's program as republican austerity, anti-corruption, poverty reduction, and empowerment of disadvantaged groups, but argued that his administration attacked judicial independence through hostile rhetoric, proposed structural changes to the Supreme Court and Federal Judicial Council, pressure over judicial salaries and appointments, media campaigns, and political threats. In 2023, Chief Justice Norma Piña defended judicial independence while pro-government militants blocked the Supreme Court after it invalidated the electoral Plan B.","question_ids":["4B.1","4B.2","4B.3","4B.4","4B.5","4B.8","4B.10","5B.1","5B.2","5B.7","6B.1","6B.3","7B.1","7B.2","7B.8","7B.10","8B.1","8B.2","8B.9","8B.10"],"polarity":"mixed","period_fit":"The analysis covers the post-2018 period and includes developments through 2023.","ruler_attribution":"The author directly attributes the austerity program, rhetoric, institutional proposals, and political pressure to López Obrador and his administration.","limitations":["This is an analytical essay relying partly on cited secondary accounts and contains interpretive judgments."]},{"source_id":"SRC-23db28d3b9616e2d","start_unit":2,"end_unit":4,"fact_summary":"López Obrador submitted a package of reforms to ease state megaproj­ects by allowing construction before all permits, facilitating unilateral contract termination, limiting indemnities, revoking private concessions, and granting broad executive powers to state entities and armed-forces-managed companies. Supporters described the reforms as restoring state capacity and combating monopolies; business and legal analysts warned of discretion, weaker provider protections, treaty and rule-of-law risks, reduced investment, and possible electoral pressure on suppliers.","question_ids":["4B.2","4B.4","4B.9","5B.1","5B.3","5B.4","5B.5","5B.6","5B.7","5B.9","7B.8","7B.9","8B.1","8B.2","8B.3","8B.5","8B.6","8B.9"],"polarity":"mixed","period_fit":"Directly concerns the reform package proposed and debated in April 2023; many measures were proposals rather than implemented law.","ruler_attribution":"The package was signed and submitted by López Obrador's executive government, with stated goals attributed to it.","limitations":["The article does not establish final enactment or implementation of the full package."]},{"source_id":"SRC-f7095e3fa232f6b8","start_unit":2,"end_unit":4,"fact_summary":"Amnesty reported that authorities criminalized protest and expression, environmental defenders faced charges and killings, journalists and defenders remained at risk, femicides and disappearances remained high, and the judiciary and migrants faced serious rights violations. The Supreme Court restricted immigration detention to 36 hours and decriminalization of abortion advanced, while the court also invalidated military control of the Guardia Nacional; the Executive continued seeking military control and environmental law was not effectively enforced on the Mayan Train.","question_ids":["3B.1","3B.3","3B.4","3B.5","3B.7","3B.8","3B.9","3B.10","4B.3","4B.4","4B.6","4B.10","6B.3","6B.8","7B.2","7B.6","7B.7","8B.6","8B.8","8B.9"],"polarity":"mixed","period_fit":"This is a 2023 human-rights report published in 2024.","ruler_attribution":"The report attributes the Executive's military, environmental, migration, and institutional positions to López Obrador's government, while some improvements came through independent court decisions.","limitations":["The report covers Mexico broadly and does not assign every violation to the president personally."]},{"source_id":"SRC-d9a1c4054c5ca065","start_unit":4,"end_unit":6,"fact_summary":"Human Rights Watch reported modest poverty reduction but unchanged extreme poverty and a more-than-doubled population lacking health access. It also documented persistent impunity, torture, arbitrary detention, military abuses, Pegasus surveillance, obstruction of Ayotzinapa investigations, attacks on journalists, inadequate protection programs, migrant detention deaths, and executive pressure on transparency institutions. Countervailing developments included disability-rights reforms, ratification of an older-persons convention, expanded asylum capacity, and Mexico's support for several international human-rights scrutiny initiatives.","question_ids":["3B.1","3B.2","3B.4","3B.5","3B.6","3B.7","3B.8","3B.9","3B.10","4B.3","4B.4","4B.6","4B.7","4B.9","4B.10","5B.8","5B.9","5B.10","6B.2","6B.3","6B.5","6B.6","6B.8","6B.9","6B.10","7B.2","7B.6","7B.7","7B.10","8B.6","8B.7","8B.8","8B.9","8B.10"],"polarity":"mixed","period_fit":"Reports events and indicators from 2023, with some historical or 2022 comparison data.","ruler_attribution":"The report directly attributes executive military, transparency, migration, social, and international policies to López Obrador's government; court and congressional reforms are not necessarily personally directed by him.","limitations":["Several indicators are national or institutional and cannot isolate presidential causation."]}],"documents_with_no_material_fact":[],"batch_limitations":["The supplied sources are uneven in timing: several concern 2023 directly, while others provide 2022 or longer-period context relevant to the 2023 ruler-period.","Facts are extracted from the supplied documents only; no scoring or cross-source adjudication is performed.","Some reported allegations, audit findings, and expert assessments were not final judicial determinations."]}
